chunks: They will say: 'We remained (in the grave or in the world) for a day or part of a day. Ask the enumerators (of days/numbers).'
ai.seo_question: What did the disbelievers say about the duration of their stay when questioned on the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: In this verse, the disbelievers attempt to minimize their accountability by claiming their earthly sojourn was fleeting, a mere day or part of a day, and challenge God to consult the 'al-'addin' (those who keep count). Shia exegetes, such as Al-Tabarsi, often interpret 'al-'addin' as the angels recording deeds or the truthful witnesses, highlighting the contrast between human subjective perception of time and the precise, objective reality known to the Divine. This moment underscores the futility of their excuse, as the brevity they claim is ultimately insignificant compared to the eternal duration of their punishment.
